name: MAKARA

variants.depicted: The complete Ganapati Sthapati source version of the Makara, a living fish-bodied elephant-trunked lion-footed monkey-eyed pig-eared peacock-tailed guardian.
variants.anatomy: ONE living hybrid creature, exactly ONE head, TWO monkey-like forward-facing intelligent eyes with rounded brow sockets, TWO clearly PIG ears folded into pointed porcine ear flaps, ONE long ELEPHANT TRUNK raised and curled toward viewer, a large scaly FISH BODY, FOUR sturdy limbs ending in unmistakable LION FEET with paw pads and natural toes, and ONE PEACOCK TAIL with feather eyespots fully unfurled at its rear. All SIX source components large and distinct: fish body, elephant trunk, lion feet, monkey eyes, pig ears, peacock tail. No crocodile jaw, elephant fan ears, fish tail fin replacing peacock, horns, tusks, wings or armour. [makara-c15]
variants.moment: Stride forward from a dark sacred gateway, one lion forepaw planted heavily in the foreground and the other lifted, trunk raised toward the viewer, intelligent eyes intent and protective, peacock feather tail sweeps in one living fan behind. Never a statue or ornamental carving.
variants.power: No documented supernatural visual power. Sacred guardian presence comes from the striking complete hybrid anatomy and decisive protective movement; a few dust grains only from the paws meeting stone. No energy streams, water spell or fire. [makara-c03, makara-c15]
variants.setting: At the threshold of an ancient temple gateway which Makara protects; architecture minimal and dark, creature dominates. [makara-c03]
variants.camera: Low-angle close three-quarter composition with entire head/trunk/ears/eyes large in upper foreground, one LION PAW huge at bottom, fish scales readable along flank, full peacock tail clear behind to one side. All required animal components visible, no tiny tail cut off.
variants.light: One warm low sunlight from outside the doorway lights wet-dark fish scales, matte paw fur and iridescent peacock feathers; deep temple shadow behind, no flame lantern or glow.

requirements.description: Complete Ganapati Sthapati c15 variant: fish body, elephant trunk, lion feet, monkey eyes, pig ears and peacock tail; no traits imported from other variants.
Protective forward movement only, no documented supernatural visual power.

variants.depicted: The coherent terrestrial-front/aquatic-rear source version of Makara: elephant front half and fish rear half, surging from the sea.
variants.anatomy: ONE living hybrid with a complete ELEPHANT FRONT HALF: ONE elephant head, TWO elephant eyes, TWO broad ELEPHANT EARS, ONE elephant trunk, TWO elephant forelegs ending in ELEPHANT FEET; the rear half is ONE elongated scaly FISH BODY with fins and ONE clearly forked FISH TAIL. No hind elephant legs, lion paws, monkey eyes, pig ears, peacock feathers, crocodile jaw, wings, horns or extra tail. No elephant tusks added. This is c12 elephant-front/fish-rear, entirely separate from Ganapati's c15 variant. [makara-c12]
variants.moment: Surge diagonally up out of the near water, trunk curling forward and two elephant forefeet braced at the rocky water edge, long scaly fish rear bending across the foreground as the fish tail throws a physical fan of spray. Elephant eyes intent and majestic, a sacred vehicle creature.
variants.power: No magic water control. Moving through its sea habitat physically displaces water into natural splash around fish tail and forefeet; not a flood, floating spell or aura. [makara-c01, makara-c09, makara-c12]
variants.setting: Immediate coastal sea water suitable for Makara the sea creature and Varuna's water-monster vehicle; no Varuna figure added. [makara-c01, makara-c09]
variants.camera: Full-body diagonal composition from extreme low waterline, head/trunk in near upper foreground, TWO elephant forefeet clear, complete fish rear and forked tail visible curling across lower side. Creature occupies most of square, no ordinary elephant on shore.
variants.light: One warm amber horizon light catches wet elephant skin and heavy fish scales; dark walnut rock shadow, pale natural spray with deep contrast.

rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
